name: xlide
description: Office VBA and Visual Basic 6 in VS Code - Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Access and .vbp projects; project tree, module editing, UserForm and VB6 form designers, static analysis, unit tests, AI agent tools

virtualWorkspaces.description: Editing, analysis and refactoring work on a workbook in a virtual workspace. Running VBA unit tests, opening the file in Excel, Word, PowerPoint or Access, and the git change marks all need a local file and a desktop editor.

xlide.officeIntegration.attachToRunning.description: Windows only: when opening a file or running a macro, try to attach to a running instance of the file's application (Excel, Word or Access) and reuse an already-open copy of the file before opening it again. PowerPoint only ever runs one instance. Turned off, every open and F5 starts another instance, and in Word and Access each one keeps the file locked until you close it.

xlide.attachToRunningExcel.deprecationMessage: Renamed to xlide.officeIntegration.attachToRunning. The value here still applies until that setting is given one.

xlide.officeIntegration.coordinationMode.description: Windows only: what XLIDE does when a file is open for editing in its application - Excel, Word, PowerPoint or Access - which locks it, during a module save, add, rename or delete, or F5 Run Macro at Cursor. 'block' (default, safest): refuse and ask you to close it in its application. 'closeTracked': gracefully close the file (without saving the application's stale copy) in instances XLIDE opened, then proceed. 'closeForce': close the file in any running instance, force-quitting the application if it will not close (unsafe; can lose unsaved work in its other open files). Under every mode XLIDE closes and reopens a READ-ONLY copy it opened itself, which holds nothing to lose: Word and PowerPoint lock a file even when it is open read-only, so a save after F5 depends on it.

xlide.excelIntegration.coordinationMode.deprecationMessage: Renamed to xlide.officeIntegration.coordinationMode. The value here still applies until that setting is given one.

xlide.officeIntegration.reopenAfterClose.description: Windows only: after XLIDE closes a file in its application to write to it (a module save, add, rename, or delete), reopen the file afterward so your view is restored. Turn off to leave it closed until you reopen it yourself. (F5 Run Macro at Cursor always reopens the file to run, and the Open commands open in the mode you picked; neither is affected by this setting.)

xlide.excelIntegration.reopenAfterClose.deprecationMessage: Renamed to xlide.officeIntegration.reopenAfterClose. The value here still applies until that setting is given one.

xlide.officeIntegration.reopenMode.description: Windows only: how XLIDE reopens a file it closed when 'Reopen After Close' is on. 'lastState' (default) puts it back the way it was, so read-only stays read-only and editable stays editable. 'readOnly' always reopens read-only. 'readWrite' reopens for editing, which locks the file again (the next XLIDE save must close it again). Access has no read-only open, so a database always reopens for editing. F5 always reopens read-only where the application allows it, regardless of this setting.

xlide.excelIntegration.reopenMode.deprecationMessage: Renamed to xlide.officeIntegration.reopenMode. The value here still applies until that setting is given one.

xlide.officeIntegration.reopenReadOnlyAf.description: Windows only: when a workbook is open READ-ONLY in Excel, a module save still writes the file (a read-only open in Excel does not lock it), but Excel keeps showing its older copy. Turn this on to have XLIDE silently close and reopen the read-only copy after each save so the view matches the saved file. Only acts when the file is actually open read-only; never reopens a file you closed, and never affects a file open for editing. Word and PowerPoint lock the file even when it is read-only, so there XLIDE closes and reopens its own read-only copy around every save regardless of this setting.

xlide.excelIntegration.reopenReadOnlyAft.deprecationMessage: Renamed to xlide.officeIntegration.reopenReadOnlyAfterSave. The value here still applies until that setting is given one.

xlide.officeIntegration.trackOpenedFiles.description: Windows only: when the coordination mode is 'closeTracked', only close files XLIDE itself opened. Turn off to close a matching file in any running instance of its application (including ones you opened manually). Ignored for 'block' and 'closeForce'.

xlide.excelIntegration.trackOpenedWorkbo.deprecationMessage: Renamed to xlide.officeIntegration.trackOpenedFiles. The value here still applies until that setting is given one.

xlide.agent.showWriteDiffs.description: When an AI agent writes a VBA module through the XLIDE tools, open a before/after diff of the change and badge the module in the XLIDE tree with Keep / Revert actions. Agent tool writes never pass through the editor, so without this no diff appears anywhere.

xlide.diagnostics.enabled.description: Show live VBA diagnostics (structural block-balance plus high-confidence semantic checks: unterminated strings, duplicate declarations, assignment to a constant, and the Option Explicit reminder).

xlide.analysis.visibleSeverities.description: Global default analysis finding severities for files that do not define a file-specific value for this setting.

xlide.analysis.ignoreFilesOutsideTree.description: Analyze only the modules the XLIDE tree lists: the ones inside a workbook, document, presentation or database, and the files a VB6 project names. A .bas, .cls or .frm on disk that no project claims, such as an exported copy, is not analyzed, so its findings do not repeat the real module's in the Problems panel. Completion, hover and navigation still work in those files. Turn off to analyze them as standalone modules.

xlide.analysis.ruleSeverityOverrides.description: Global default guarded rule severity overrides keyed by analysis rule code. Warning and information rules can be set to 'off'; only rules marked downgrade-safe can be set from error to 'warning'.

xlide.analysis.untrackedRules.description: Global default analysis diagnostic rule codes hidden from tracking for files that do not define a file-specific value for this setting.

xlide.editor.blockLayout.description: Controls VBA Smart Enter and block-snippet layout. 'comfy' inserts spacer lines around the editable body; 'compact' places the editable body directly above the closer.

xlide.editor.continueCommentOnNewline.description: When the line above is a VBA comment (starts with an apostrophe), pressing Enter begins the new line with an apostrophe to continue the comment. Turn off for a plain new line with no apostrophe.

xlide.editor.mirrorCommentSpacing.description: When continuing a comment, copy the run of spaces that follows the apostrophe on the line above so the text lines up. Turn off to insert just the apostrophe with no space. Only applies when 'Continue Comment On New Line' is on.

xlide.explorer.autoExpandCollapse.description: Automatically reveal the active module in the XLIDE explorer and collapse the others as you switch editor tabs (a one-file, one-module accordion). Turn off to leave the tree as you arrange it - switching tabs and expanding nodes will not auto-collapse anything.

xlide.explorer.view.description: How the XLIDE explorer arranges a project's modules. Tree lists them flat. Folders groups them by the '@Folder("Name.Sub")' comment in each module's declarations, the Rubberduck convention. The Tree and Folders buttons above the explorer switch it too.

xlide.docs.enabled.description: Enrich VBA hovers and call tips with developer-defined XML documentation: '''-comments above your procedures and external metadata files found in the workspace.

xlide.docs.metadataGlob.description: Glob (relative to each workspace folder) that locates external VBA documentation metadata files. These describe symbols using the same XML vocabulary as '''-comments and override the built-in curated library.

xlide.performance.trace.description: Write slow XLIDE performance trace events to the XLIDE output channel. Recent timings are always available from the Copy Performance Snapshot command.

xlide.formRun.injectShowMacro.description: When F5 launches a UserForm in an Excel, Word or PowerPoint file, XLIDE can add a small launcher macro to the file - one sub per form, all in module XlideRun - and run it so the form opens immediately, the way F5 in the VBE does. Ask (default): confirm the first time a form needs its launcher; once that sub exists F5 just runs it, with no prompt. Always: add and show without asking. Never: F5 just opens the file. The subs stay in the file and are safe to delete. An Access form or report needs no launcher: Access opens it by name, so nothing is added to the database.

colors.description: Colour of a module an AI agent edited, and of the project and folders that hold it, in the XLIDE tree until the edit is kept or reverted.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No macro-enabled Office files (.xlsm, .xlsb, .xlam, .xltm, .xls, .docm, .dotm, .doc, .pptm, .potm, .ppsm, .ppt, .accdb, .mdb, and their template/add-in variants) were found in the current workspace.
[Refresh](command:xlide.refreshExplorer)

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listProjects
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Finds all macro-enabled Office files in the current workspace and returns their absolute paths: Excel (.xlsm, .xlsb, .xlam, .xltm, .xls, .xlt, .xla), Word (.docm, .dotm, .doc, .dot), PowerPoint (.pptm, .potm, .ppsm, .ppam, .ppt, .ppa), and Access (.accdb, .accda, .mdb, .mda). Visual Basic 6 projects (.vbp) are listed too; their modules are the .bas, .cls and .frm files the manifest names. Call this first when the user has not specified a file path, or when you need to discover which files are available.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_getProjectInfo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a combined one-shot summary of a macro-enabled Office file: VBA modules (name + type), worksheets (name + used dimensions), and named ranges. Sheets and named ranges are populated for OOXML Excel workbooks only; for Word, PowerPoint, Access, and legacy .xls files those arrays are empty even though the file may have its own non-worksheet content. Treat the file/XLIDE virtual modules as the source of truth for VBA. Use this as the first discovery call instead of calling xlide_listModules and xlide_listSheets separately.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

languageModelTools.name: xlide_validateProject
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks a macro-enabled Office file's VBA project (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) for cross-structure inconsistencies and returns {issues: [...]}. An empty issues array means the project is structurally sound. Use this to audit a file before or after edits.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

languageModelTools.name: xlide_analyzeProject
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Analyzes every VBA module in a macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) using XLIDE's VBA syntax and structural analyzer - the SAME high-confidence, false-positive-free rule engine that powers the live editor diagnostics, letting an agent VERIFY THAT ANALYSIS PASSES IN REAL TIME. Returns a JSON report: {filePath, moduleCount, errorCount, warningCount, problems: [{moduleName, moduleType, line, column, severity, code, message}]}. An empty problems array means the file's VBA passes analysis. Use this after writing or editing modules (e.g. after xlide_writeModule) or to audit an entire file. Covers block-balance, unterminated strings, duplicate declarations, Const assignment, malformed procedure headers, argument-count mismatches, unbalanced parentheses, Sub/Function-not-defined and more - each carrying an MS-VBAL spec reference. Complements XLIDE's inline ''' XML doc-comments and external *.vbref.xml metadata files, which enrich hovers and call tips for the symbols this analyzer checks. Pass moduleName to analyze just one module after editing it.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm (or .xlsb / .xlam) file to analyze

moduleName.description: Optional single module to analyze. Use this to check one module you just edited instead of re-analyzing the whole project.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_runVbaTests
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs discovered '@xlide-test' VBA tests through XLIDE's production owned read-only test host in the file's own application (Excel for workbooks, Word for documents, PowerPoint for presentations, Access for databases), writes the same timestamped artifacts/status_for_ci.json as the Tests GUI, and returns JSON {ok, summary, artifacts, report}. Use this after editing VBA to verify tests pass without opening the Tests GUI. Requires the file to have the current XlideAssert.bas support module installed and the matching Office application's COM to be available. Supports narrowing by moduleName, procedureName, testIds, includeTags, excludeTags, and failFast. Set includeHostEvents true only when diagnosing host/oracle behavior.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm (or .xlsb / .xlam) file to test

moduleName.description: Optional VBA standard module name to restrict discovery

procedureName.description: Optional test Sub procedure name to run

testIds.description: Optional exact XLIDE test ids to run

includeTags.description: Optional tags; when present, only tests with at least one matching tag run

excludeTags.description: Optional tags to exclude from the run

failFast.description: Stop after the first failed, timed out, host-error, or unexpected-pass result

includeHostEvents.description: Include low-level test host oracle events in the JSON response for debugging

languageModelTools.name: xlide_createProject
languageModelTools.displayName: Create New Project File or Add-In
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Creates a new macro-enabled file with an empty VBA project at the given absolute path: an Excel workbook, template or add-in (.xlsm, .xlsb, .xltm, .xlam), a Word document or template (.docm, .dotm), a PowerPoint presentation or template (.pptm, .potm), or an Access database or add-in (.accdb, .accda, .mdb, .mda). The extension of filePath selects the format; each format comes from a genuine Office-authored template, never a renamed container. Legacy formats (.xls/.doc/.ppt) cannot be created. Fails if the file already exists; it never overwrites an existing file.

filePath.description: Absolute path for the new file; the extension selects the format (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam, .docm/.dotm, .pptm/.potm)

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listModules
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists all VBA modules in a macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) or a Visual Basic 6 project (.vbp). Returns module names and types (standard, class, document, userform; a VB6 project may also list usercontrol, propertypage and designer), and the module's `@Folder` annotation when it carries one. Use this before reading or editing that file's VBA; do not infer module state from exported .bas/.cls repo files, which can be stale, unless the user explicitly asks to work on those export artifacts.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listSubs
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists all Sub and Function procedures in a specific VBA module. Returns procedure names, kinds (Sub/Function/Property Get/Let/Set), and line numbers.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm file

languageModelTools.name: xlide_readModule
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Canonical way to read VBA source. Reads the full source of a module from the macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) and returns raw VBA text including Attribute declarations. These files are binary containers, not text - always read VBA through this tool or through the XLIDE virtual file system (modules opened from the XLIDE tree are live module documents at xlide-vba:// URIs), never by opening the container file directly. Do not read exported .bas/.cls/.frm files in the project as a substitute, even when they look current: they are one-way artifacts and can be stale. Read those only when the user explicitly asks about the export artifacts themselves. Returns a contentToken on the first line: pass it back as expectedContentToken when writing so the write is refused if the module changed in the meantime. Use startLine/endLine to read part of a very large module.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm file

moduleName.description: Name of the VBA module to read

startLine.description: Optional 1-based first line to return. Use with endLine to read part of a large module instead of the whole thing; the reported contentToken still describes the WHOLE module.

endLine.description: Optional 1-based last line to return, inclusive.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_writeModule
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Canonical way to edit VBA. Writes VBA source directly into the macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access; Access runs the compiled project, so a write there takes effect when Access next opens the database and recompiles) and saves automatically. These files are binary containers, so VBA changes persist only through XLIDE. Make every change with this tool, even to a module the user has open: modules opened from the XLIDE tree are live xlide-vba:// documents, and an edit made to one with a generic file-edit tool is saved into the file without XLIDE's review - the user gets no before/after diff and no tree badge for it. Edit such a document directly only when the user asks you to. Never edit the container file with generic file/text tools, and do not write exported .bas/.cls/.frm files in the project as a way of changing VBA - those are one-way artifacts that no host reads back, so editing one changes nothing. Touch them only when the user explicitly asks. Creates the module if it does not exist (optionally pass kind='class'; default is standard). IMPORTANT: Use only ASCII characters to avoid character mangling - no Unicode, emoji, or accented characters. Pass expectedContentToken from the read you based this edit on: without it, a change made by the host application or a user after your read is overwritten silently. After a chat-driven write, XLIDE shows the user a before/after diff and badges the module in its tree with Keep/Revert actions until they decide (xlide.agent.showWriteDiffs). A revert restores the pre-write source, or removes a module this write created, so if the user mentions reverting, re-read the module before editing further.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm file

moduleName.description: Name of the VBA module to write

source.description: The full VBA source code to write into the module

expectedContentToken.description: Optional contentToken from the xlide_readModule that this edit is based on. When supplied, the write is refused if the module changed since that read, instead of silently discarding the change.

kind.description: What a module this call creates is: 'class' for a class module, 'standard' (the default) for a standard module. A module that already exists keeps its kind; passing the other kind for one is refused.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_renameModule
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renames a VBA module in a macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) and saves it. Operates on the live XLIDE module - do not rename the container file or its exported .bas/.cls files to rename a module. Use this to change a module's name. After renaming, any references to the old name in other modules must be updated manually with xlide_writeModule. A document module (ThisWorkbook, a sheet module, ThisDocument) cannot be renamed: its name is also the code name its document keeps.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

moduleName.description: Current name of the VBA module

newName.description: New name for the VBA module

languageModelTools.name: xlide_deleteModule
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Permanently deletes a VBA module from a macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) and saves it. Operates on the live XLIDE module - do not delete the container file or its exported .bas/.cls files to remove a module. This cannot be undone. Only delete standard or class modules; document modules (such as ThisWorkbook, a sheet module, or ThisDocument) cannot be deleted.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

moduleName.description: Name of the VBA module to delete

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listSheets
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists all worksheet names and their used cell ranges (dimensions) in an Excel file. Call this first whenever the sheet name is unknown before using xlide_readCells, xlide_readFormulas, xlide_writeCells, or xlide_editShape. Returns an array of {name, dimensions} objects where dimensions is in A1 notation (e.g. 'A1:D20') or empty for a blank sheet.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

languageModelTools.name: xlide_readCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads computed cell values (not formulas) from a worksheet in an Excel file. Returns a 2D array of values (rows x columns). If the sheet name is unknown, call xlide_listSheets first. To read raw formulas instead, use xlide_readFormulas. Formula results are the ones Excel last calculated: after xlide_writeCells, the written formulas read as null and the formulas that depend on changed cells keep their old results until the workbook is next opened in Excel, which recalculates it.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm file

range.description: Cell range in A1 notation, e.g. 'A1:D10'

languageModelTools.name: xlide_readFormulas
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads raw cell content including formula strings (e.g. '=SUM(A1:A10)') from a worksheet. Use this instead of xlide_readCells when you need to understand or reproduce spreadsheet logic. Returns a 2D array; formula cells contain the formula string, non-formula cells contain their value. Formulas read as Excel shows them: =XLOOKUP(...) rather than the file's _xlfn.XLOOKUP(...), F2# for a spill range, and each cell of a shared formula with its own references. The cells a dynamic array spills into, and the cells of an array formula after its first, hold values.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm file

range.description: Cell range in A1 notation, e.g. 'A1:D10'

languageModelTools.name: xlide_writeCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Writes values to a range of cells in a worksheet in an Excel file. The file is saved automatically. If the sheet name is unknown, call xlide_listSheets first. A string starting with = is a formula, written as you would type it into Excel 365: =XLOOKUP(...), =FILTER(...) and =SEQUENCE(...) work without prefixes, and a formula whose result is an array spills. Each formula is checked as Excel checks a typed one (argument counts, references, sheet and table names), and if Excel would reject any of them nothing is written and the error names the cell and the problem. Written cells keep their formatting, and new cells take their row's or column's. Writing part of an array formula is refused; a value inside a spill range blocks the spill (#SPILL!), as in Excel. Excel recalculates the workbook the next time it opens it. IMPORTANT: Use only ASCII characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and standard ASCII punctuation) to avoid character mangling. Avoid Unicode, emoji, accented characters, and special symbols.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm file

startCell.description: Top-left cell in A1 notation, e.g. 'A1'

data.description: 2D array of values to write (rows of columns)

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listReferences
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the type libraries a VBA project references, as the VBE Tools > References dialog shows them: the name the project knows each by, whether it is a registered library, another VBA project or a control, and the libid, which carries the library GUID, its version and the path it was registered at. A project that references another Office application can name that application types, so this is what says whether Excel.Application means anything in a Word document; XLIDE analyzes such a module against both object models. Call this to find out which applications a project drives, before reading code that names one. A VB6 project keeps its references in the .vbp manifest and answers with an empty list.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file

languageModelTools.name: xlide_addReference
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds a reference to another Office application's type library to a VBA project, the way the VBE Tools > References dialog does. A project needs one to name that application's types early bound: without it, Dim xl As Excel.Application in a Word document does not compile ("User-defined type not defined") and the whole project stops compiling, which is what XLIDE reports as missing-library-reference. Use it when code names a library the project does not reference; call xlide_listReferences first to see what it already has. Late binding - Dim x As Object with CreateObject("Excel.Application") - needs no reference at all, so prefer that where the code should run without one. The libraries that can be added are excel, word, powerpoint and access. Adding one the project already has changes nothing. A VB6 project keeps its references in the .vbp manifest, which XLIDE does not write.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file

library.description: The application whose object library to reference

languageModelTools.name: xlide_removeReference
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Removes a type-library reference from a VBA project, as unchecking it in the VBE Tools > References dialog does. Name the library as xlide_listReferences reports it (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Access, Office, stdole, MSForms, or another project). Code that still names the library early bound stops compiling the moment the reference goes - the VBE reports "User-defined type not defined" and the whole project stops compiling - so read the modules first and rewrite them to late binding, or leave the reference alone. Removing one the project does not have changes nothing. Microsoft Forms is refused while the project still has a UserForm, which cannot be instantiated without it. A VB6 project keeps its references in the .vbp manifest, which XLIDE does not write.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file

library.description: The reference to remove, named as xlide_listReferences reports it

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listShapes
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the shapes on the surfaces of a macro-enabled Office file: a worksheet in Excel, a slide in PowerPoint, or a story in Word (the body, each header and each footer). Covers AutoShapes, text boxes, pictures, charts, groups, PowerPoint placeholders, Word drawing canvases, and Excel form controls (buttons, check boxes, drop-downs, ...) and ActiveX controls. For each shape it returns its name, kind, and when set its geometry, its macro (the Sub a click runs, as Proc or Module.Proc), text, alt text and whether it is hidden; a group or canvas lists its members in shapes. Excel reports the cells a shape covers as range; Word and PowerPoint report left, top, width and height in points, and Word also reports placement (inline with the text, or anchored). Omit surface to list every surface. Call this before xlide_editShape to learn shape and surface names, and to find which Subs a file wires to its shapes. Word shapes cannot run macros at all, and Excel ActiveX controls run event procedures in the sheet module (such as CommandButton1_Click) rather than a macro.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled file: an Excel workbook (.xlsm/.xlam/...), a Word document (.docm/.dotm) or a PowerPoint presentation (.pptm/.potm/.ppsm)

surface.description: The surface to list: a worksheet name in Excel, a slide in PowerPoint (its name, or its position as 'Slide 2'), or a story in Word ('Document', 'Header', 'Footer', 'First Page Header', ...). Omit to list every surface.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_editShape
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds, changes or deletes one shape on a surface of a macro-enabled Office file, and links shapes to macros. The file is saved automatically. Works on an Excel worksheet, a PowerPoint slide, and a Word story (the body, a header or a footer). action add needs type (rectangle, roundedRectangle, oval, textBox, or button for an Excel form-control button) and a position: in Excel, range, the cells the shape covers such as 'B2:D3'; in PowerPoint, left and top in points (width and height default to 120 by 60); in Word, left and top make it a floating shape, and omitting both makes it inline with the text. name, text, macro and altText are optional, and the result gives the name the host would have picked when name is left out. action update changes the named shape: range (Excel) or left, top, width and height (Word and PowerPoint) move or resize it, text sets its text, macro sets the Sub a click runs, linkedCell and inputRange set an Excel form control's cell link and list, altText sets its alt text, newName renames it; properties left out stay as they are, and an empty string removes a macro, cell link, list or alt text. action delete removes the named shape. A macro is a Public Sub with no required parameters, given as Proc or Module.Proc, and it must already exist in the VBA project, so write the Sub first with xlide_writeModule. WORD CANNOT RUN A MACRO FROM A SHAPE - its shapes have no OnAction and no ActionSettings, and the file format has nowhere to keep one - so use macro only on Excel and PowerPoint. Pictures and charts are listed, moved, renamed and deleted but cannot be added, since that needs image or data bytes. Call xlide_listShapes first for shape and surface names. Excel ActiveX controls are listed but not edited, and a shape inside a group or a Word drawing canvas is moved or deleted with its container. IMPORTANT: Use only ASCII characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and standard ASCII punctuation) to avoid character mangling. Avoid Unicode, emoji, accented characters, and special symbols.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled file: an Excel workbook (.xlsm/.xlam/...), a Word document (.docm/.dotm) or a PowerPoint presentation (.pptm/.potm/.ppsm)

surface.description: The surface the shape is on: a worksheet name in Excel, a slide in PowerPoint (its name, or its position as 'Slide 2'), or a story in Word ('Document', 'Header', 'Footer', ...). Required for Excel and PowerPoint; in Word it defaults to 'Document'.

action.description: add a new shape, update the named shape, or delete it

name.description: The shape to update or delete, or the new shape's name (optional for add)

type.description: What to add; button is an Excel form-control button

range.description: Excel only: the cells the shape covers, e.g. 'B2:D3'

left.description: Points from the left edge, for a Word or PowerPoint shape

top.description: Points from the top edge, for a Word or PowerPoint shape

width.description: Width in points, for a Word or PowerPoint shape

height.description: Height in points, for a Word or PowerPoint shape

text.description: The shape's text or the control's caption; \n starts a new line

macro.description: The Public Sub a click runs, as Proc or Module.Proc; an empty string removes it. Excel and PowerPoint only - a Word shape cannot run a macro

linkedCell.description: Excel form control only: its cell link, e.g. '$H$10' or 'Sheet2!$H$10'; an empty string removes it

inputRange.description: Excel drop-down or list box only: the cells it lists, e.g. '$J$1:$J$5'; an empty string removes them

altText.description: Alt text; an empty string removes it

newName.description: A new name for the shape

languageModelTools.name: xlide_exportModules
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Exports all VBA modules from a macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) to a folder using <file>.xlide_settings.json behavior shared with UI commands. This is a sync/export operation, not the primary agent editing surface: read and write module code through xlide_readModule/xlide_writeModule unless the user explicitly asks to manage exported repo files. Uses live module reads from the file. Supports exportMode exportAll (default: export every module, no deletes) and trueUp (export every module, then remove stale .bas/.cls module files missing from the file).

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

exportFolder.description: Optional absolute folder path. If omitted, uses the project-specific exportFolder from <file>.xlide_settings.json

exportMode.description: Optional mode override for this run

languageModelTools.name: xlide_configureExportMode
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sets the persistent per-file exportMode in <file>.xlide_settings.json beside the macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access). Use exportAll by default unless the user explicitly asks to delete stale .bas/.cls module files missing from the file.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

exportMode.description: Persistent project-specific export mode to store in <file>.xlide_settings.json

languageModelTools.name: xlide_searchModules
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches the VBA source of every module in a macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) and returns the matching lines with their module name and 1-based line number. Use this instead of reading every module to find where a name is declared or used. Case-insensitive by default.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

query.description: Text to find in module source.

isRegex.description: Treat query as a regular expression. Default false.

maxResults.description: Cap on returned matches. Default 200; the reply says when results were capped.

languageModelTools.userDescription: Search across all VBA modules in a macro-enabled file

languageModelTools.name: xlide_gitChanges
languageModelTools.displayName: VBA Changes Since a Git Revision
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists what changed inside a macro-enabled Office file (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or Access) since a git revision, HEAD by default: one entry per module that was modified, added, or removed, each with a unified diff of the module's VBA (the committed module on the left, the file on disk on the right). Git itself can only say that the whole file changed, so use this to review a change, summarize it, or write a commit message for a file. Answers with tracked:false and a reason when the file is outside a repository, not tracked by git, or absent at the revision. Pass moduleName to get one module's diff, or revision (a commit hash, tag, or branch) to compare against something other than HEAD.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the macro-enabled Office file (.xlsm/.xlsb/.xlam/.xls, .docm/.dotm/.doc, .pptm/.potm/.ppsm/.ppt, .accdb/.mdb)

revision.description: Optional git revision to compare the file on disk with: a commit hash, tag, or branch. Default HEAD.

moduleName.description: Optional single module to report. Default: every module that differs.
